zh: 这本书是一份爱的劳作，而这份爱因认识到以下一点而愈发深厚：罗马尽管壮丽，却也充分乃至有时悲剧性地浸透着人类境况的一切弱点。我父母第一次带我去罗马时，我还是个学童；他们让我的一生铭刻下对这座非凡城市的热情，这份热情随着岁月有增无减。我试图传达这种强烈的情感，也传达罗马人辛辣的幽默和绚丽的建筑狂热、严酷的社会现实和温暖的合群之道、他们生活中动人的脆弱，以及他们面对失望与兴奋时所表现出的巍然力量和自信。我在书中写到的罗马城区蒙蒂，曾欢迎我进入一个深深打上这些人类维度烙印的世界。任何人类学家、任何学者——事实上，任何有感知力的人——都不可能再向任何一个地方要求更多。
en: This book is the labor of a love deepened by the realization that Rome, despite its magnificence, is also splendidly, sometimes tragically, a place steeped in all the weaknesses of the human condition. My parents first took me there when I was a schoolboy and marked my life with a passion for this extraordinary place that has only grown with the years. I have tried to convey this powerful affect, along with the Romans’ salty humor and gorgeous architectural frenzies, their harsh social realities and their warm gregariousness, the appealing fragility of their lives and the towering strength and self-confidence with which they meet its disappointments as well as its excitements. Monti, the sector of Rome about which I write in these pages, welcomed me to a world strongly marked by these human dimensions. No anthropologist, no scholar—indeed, no sentient human being—could ask for more of any place.

zh: 在这项工作中，许多人各尽其力。列举名单容易招怨，而且肯定会漏掉某个人，因为热忱支持我项目的人实在太多；也因为我与他们的许多谈话至今仍在继续，有时短暂中断，但总是执拗地回到共同热爱的主题上。不过，有几个人付出了格外持久的努力，我要记录我对他们建议、洞见和支持的感激：洛雷达娜·阿卡、保罗·贝尔迪尼、卡洛·切拉马雷、阿德里亚娜·戈尼、路易吉·隆巴迪·萨特里亚尼、贝拉尔迪诺·帕伦博、安德烈娜·里奇、保罗·夏罗尼、里卡多·特罗伊西，以及瓦莱里全家（文琴佐、弗朗切斯科、安德烈亚和保拉）。一些同事也就具体技术问题提供了有益建议，其中包括经济学家里卡多·豪斯曼和语言学家保罗·迪·乔维内。卡伦·亨德里克森-桑托斯帕戈把我混乱的指示变成了一幅极其清晰的地图。
en: In the work that is laid out here, many people played their parts. Lists are invidious and someone is sure to be omitted, simply because there were so many who enthusiastically supported my project; and because so many of the conversations I had with them continue to this day, sometimes briefly interrupted, but always insistently returning to the themes of a shared passion. A few people nonetheless made especially sustained efforts, and I want to record my appreciation of their counsel, insights, and support: Loredana Acca, Paolo Berdini, Carlo Cellamare, Adriana Goni, Luigi Lombardi Satriani, Berardino Palumbo, Andreina Ricci, Paolo Sciarroni, Riccardo Troisi, and the entire Valeri family (Vincenzo, Francesco, Andrea, and Paola). Certain colleagues also offered helpful advice on specific technical questions; these include the economist Ricardo Hausmann and the linguist Paolo Di Giovine. Karen Hendrickson-Santospago converted my confusing instructions into a splendidly legible map.

zh: 那些慷慨阅读书稿并提出极具洞见意见的人——奥古斯托·费拉伊乌奥洛、科妮莉亚（内娅）·迈尔·赫茨菲尔德、道格拉斯·霍姆斯、居伊·拉努、莉莉丝·阿卜杜勒瓦哈卜·马哈茂德、玛丽亚·米尼库奇、博登·佩因特、米里亚姆·沙考和克劳迪奥·索普兰泽蒂——尤其值得感谢。卡洛·切拉马雷和玛丽亚·米尼库奇还安排我在罗马大学（“La Sapienza”）各自所在的院系担任访问职位，并在这几年的研究中与我进行了更广泛、极富成效的讨论；内娅·赫茨菲尔德在许多地方都是我始终如一的伴侣，她在这项工作推进过程中带来了洞见和慷慨的批判眼光，还帮我巩固了我们与蒙蒂人乃至整个罗马人的许多共同友谊。在芝加哥大学出版社，我深深感谢老朋友T. 戴维·布伦特、他效率非凡的助手劳拉·J. 艾维，以及我细致、善解人意且对文体敏感的文稿编辑玛丽·格尔。还有许多其他朋友，他们的声音在本书中以不同程度显现，或沿途提供了有益建议；我对他们的亏欠同样深切，也同样广泛。
en: Those generous souls who read the manuscript and offered their extremely perceptive comments on it—Augusto Ferraiuolo, Cornelia (Nea) Mayer Herzfeld, Douglas Holmes, Guy Lanoue, Lilith Abdelwahab Mahmud, Maria Minicuci, Borden Painter, Miriam Shakow, and Claudio Sopranzetti—deserve special gratitude. Carlo Cellamare and Maria Minicuci also arranged for me to hold visiting appointments in their respective parts of the University of Rome-I (“La Sapienza”) and engaged me in larger and extraordinarily productive discussions throughout these years of research, while Nea Herzfeld, constant companion in so many places, brought insight and a generously critical eye to this work as it progressed, besides cementing many of our shared friendships with the people of Monti and of Rome in general. At the University of Chicago Press, I am deeply indebted to my old friend T. David Brent, his extraordinarily efficient assistant Laura J. Avey, and my meticulous, understanding, and stylistically sensitive manuscript editor Mary Gehl. To the many other friends whose voices are heard with varying degrees of explicitness in these pages, or who proffered useful advice along the way, my debt is as deeply felt and appreciated as it is wide-ranging.

zh: 虽然文责照例由我自负，我确实真心想感谢那些帮助我完成主要研究阶段的基金会：美国国家人文基金会和约翰·西蒙·古根海姆纪念基金会，它们先后资助了我1999—2000学年的休假研究。哈佛大学韦瑟黑德国际事务中心慷慨资助了我2007年的又一次休假，从而促成了本项目的大部分写作。我在墨尔本大学的逗留也为我提供了宝贵的休整之所。
en: While the usual provisos about personal responsibility apply, I do genuinely want to thank the foundations that helped me bring this work through the main research phase. These are the National Endowment for the Humanities and the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation, which sequentially supported my sabbatical year research in 1999-2000. Harvard University’s Weatherhead Center for International Affairs generously supported a further leave in 2007 and thereby facilitated much of the writing for this project. My sojourns at the University of Melbourne also provided me with an invaluable retreat.

zh: 所有未注明出处的引文，都是我对交谈对象言论的翻译；除不可避免的例外（如公众人物或角色受到显著关注的个人）之外，我避免使用他们的真实姓名。许多人说话时混合使用“标准语言”和“方言”；这些混合话语有时会让受过教育的本地读者感到惊讶，但它们确实代表了言语习惯（尤其是语码转换），而这些习惯本身就是社会互动中身份政治微妙却不停变动的有用证据。
en: All unattributed quotations are my translations of remarks made by informants; I have, except in the case of unavoidable exceptions (such as public figures or individuals whose role received significant attention), avoided using their own personal names. Many of them spoke in a mixture of “standard language” and “dialect,” and, while these mixed utterances have sometimes occasioned surprise on the part of educated local readers, they do represent habits of speech (notably code-switching) that are themselves useful evidence of subtly but ceaselessly shifting identity politics in social interactions.

zh: 当我开始琢磨去泰国做田野调查的念头时，我的系里同事斯坦利·J. 坦比亚——泰国研究的一位领军人物——起初表示异议，随后对这件事显露出明显的不安，直到他确信我会先研究希腊民族主义与意大利民族主义的比较。当我告诉他，我打算先去罗马，再尝试在泰国做任何实质性工作，并请他为我的一项奖学金申请写推荐信时，他立刻以那种非凡的慷慨和对我的学术生活的关怀作出回应——后来一切都清楚表明，正是这种关怀最初引发了他的担忧和犹豫。坦比亚个人的谦逊与善良，正如他的思想启发一样具有传奇色彩；简单地说，他改变了一切。他也和我一样热爱罗马这座城市。从非常真实的意义上说，本书是对他带给我们的每一次相遇的思想激励与彻底善意所作出的回应；我怀着最深、最感激的深情，将它献给他。
en: When I began to toy with the idea of doing field research in Thailand, my departmental colleague Stanley J. Tambiah, a leading light in Thai studies, at first demurred and then showed some apparent discomfort with the idea—until he was satisfied that I would first pursue my interests in the comparison of Greek and Italian nationalisms. When I told him that I intended to go to Rome before I attempted anything substantive in Thailand and asked him for a letter of support for one of my fellowship applications, he immediately responded with all the extraordinary generosity and care for my scholarly life that had, it became entirely clear, animated his original concern and hesitation. Tambi, whose personal modesty and kindness are as legendary as his intellectual inspiration, has, quite simply, made all the difference. He also shares my enthusiasm for Rome as a city. This book is, in a very real sense, a response to the combination of intellectual stimulation and radical kindness that he has brought to all our encounters, and I dedicate it to him with the deepest and most grateful affection.
